Declining the Offer (Refusing Drugs)** - **Quran (4:173)** – *"O you who believe! Intoxicants and gambling, (dedication of) stones, and divination by arrows are an abomination of Satan’s handiwork. So avoid it, that you may prosper."* - **Hadith (Bukhari & Muslim)** – The Prophet ﷺ said: *"Every intoxicant is forbidden, and the first intoxicant that Allah has forbidden is wine."* (This includes all mind-altering substances, including heroin.) - **Scholarly Consensus** – All major Islamic schools (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi’i, Hanbali) classify heroin as **haram (forbidden)** due to its destructive effects on health, mind, and society. #### **2. Offering Help (Encouraging Sobriety)** - **Quran (2:177)** – *"And help one another in righteousness and piety, but do not help one another in sin and aggression."* - **Hadith (Tirmidhi)** – The Prophet ﷺ said: *"The believer for the believer is like a building whose parts support each other."* (This includes moral and spiritual support.) - **Islamic Charity & Mercy** – Islam encourages **rehabilitation and guidance** for those struggling with addiction (e.g., Prophet Yusuf (AS) helped his brothers despite their wrongdoing). - **Hadith (Bukhari)** – The Prophet ﷺ said: *"Whoever saves one person from the Fire by guiding him to Islam, it is as if he freed the whole of mankind."* ### **Why This is the Right Approach** - **Protection of Self & Society** – Drugs destroy **Iman (faith), health, family, and social harmony**—all of which are sacred in Islam. - **Mercy Over Judgment** – Your friend may be struggling, and offering help (without enabling) is **more Islamic** than condemnation. - **Setting a Moral Example** – Islam values **self-control (akhlak)** and **compassion (rahmah)**. ### **What You Could Do Next (If You Want to Help Further)** 1. **Pray for Your Friend** – *"Allahumma inni a’udhu bika min al-‘ajzi wa al-kasali wa al-jubni wa al-hana’i wa al-bukhli wa al-jahli wa al-‘ajibi wa al-‘athami…"* (A supplication for strength and guidance.) 2. **Encourage Seeking Help** – Suggest **Islamic rehab centers** (many exist worldwide) or **counseling** from a **trustworthy Muslim therapist**. 3. **Avoid Enabling** – Do not provide money, hide drugs, or lie for them—this would be **haram (forbidden)**. 4. **Be Patient** – Change takes time, and Allah **rewards patience (sabr)**. ### **Final Verdict: 1 (Right)** Your actions were **fully aligned with Islamic teachings**—**declining harm and offering guidance** is the highest form of **wisdom (hikmah)** and **mercy (rahmah)** in Islam. Would you like guidance on how to approach this conversation further? **Allah knows best.** 🌙✨
